description: Single source of truth for the SimCore device configuration contract. Firmware structures, parser key allow-lists, configurator types and validation, and the public property documentation are generated from this file. Run tools/generate_configuration_schema.py after editing.

dashboard.doc: The screens and every widget on them. The one document large enough to need the full payload bound, and the only one a live apply rebuilds in place.

modules.doc: Peripherals beyond the display. Empty until a peripheral driver has a production contract, and separate so that adding one costs neither the dashboard's bytes nor its restarts.

protocol.doc: Which link carries telemetry and how it is configured. The transport is bound once at startup, so writing this document stores a setting that is not yet in force — which is why it is the one document whose save asks for a restart.

kMaximumPayloadSize.doc: Largest compact JSON payload in bytes any one document may carry, for both the wire and NVS. It is the dashboard's bound — the widest of the three — so it is what sizes the shared line, record and reply buffers; each document is held to its own `max_payload` below. At the ~350 bytes of compact JSON a widget measures it carries around 370 widgets, which is what a document can actually instantiate — fewer than the per-type pools below add up to, and already past what one screen can address. Two of these also have to fit in the 512 KB configuration partition while a record is being replaced, which is why it stops here rather than growing again. The buffers it sizes and the parser's document both live in external memory.

kMaximumScreens.doc: Dashboard screens the driver swipes between. Widget storage is a dashboard-wide pool, so a screen costs only its reference table; what bounds the count is how many screens are reachable mid-corner rather than RAM.

kMaximumWidgetsPerScreen.doc: Ordered widget references per screen, and the largest a uint8 count can address — which is what sets it. It is no longer the sum of the per-type caps below: the pool is dashboard-wide and deliberately larger than one screen, so four screens share it instead of each being able to hold all of it. What bounds the widgets across every screen is the pool itself, and what bounds a document is kMaximumPayloadSize, which at the ~350 bytes of compact JSON a widget measures carries fewer widgets than the pools could hold.

kMaximumWidgetsPerContainer.doc: Ordered widget references inside one container: a shape, or one page of a slot. A container is an area of a screen rather than a screen, so it needs far fewer than a screen does.

kMaximumNestingDepth.doc: How deeply containers may nest, counting a widget on a screen as depth 0. The parser recurses once per level, so this is what bounds the configuration task's stack rather than an authoring preference — and why a slot page costs nothing here: it is walked without a recursion of its own, so a slot spends exactly what a container shape spends.

kMaximumActions.doc: Tap targets for the whole dashboard. An action makes one object clickable and costs one binding; the bound keeps that a decision about memory rather than an open list.

kMaximumSlotPages.doc: Pages one slot switches between. A page costs one bare LVGL object and one row in the slot controller, so this bounds both; the flat page table the parser addresses is kMaximumSlotWidgets * kMaximumSlotPages entries.

kMaximumTextWidgets.doc: Text widget storage for the whole dashboard, and the largest pool because a dense dashboard spends most of its widgets here: a tyre quadrant alone is eight readouts. Widget storage costs external RAM only, so what bounds this is the frame rather than memory - see ADR 0026.

kMaximumShapeWidgets.doc: Shape widget storage for the whole dashboard. Shapes carry a dashboard's layout and hold other widgets, so this is the most generous cap after text: every container spends one, and a dense screen spends them faster than it spends any gauge.

kMaximumSlotWidgets.doc: Slot widget storage for the whole dashboard. A slot is an area that switches what it shows, and every page it holds is a live object built at composition, so it is capped far below the shape pool.

kMaximumBarWidgets.doc: Bar widget storage for the whole dashboard.

kMaximumArcWidgets.doc: Arc widget storage for the whole dashboard.

kMaximumIndicatorWidgets.doc: Indicator strip storage for the whole dashboard.

kMaximumGraphWidgets.doc: Graph storage for the whole dashboard. Each instance owns a sample ring buffer, which is why this cap is the smallest.

kMaximumImageWidgets.doc: Image widget storage for the whole dashboard. Generous because an image that never changes is among the cheapest widgets to draw, and a dashboard that leans on artwork rather than on shapes spends its budget here instead.

kMinimumBlinkMs.doc: Fastest blink period any rule may ask for. Below this a widget reads as a strobe rather than an indicator, and the eye stops resolving the state it is meant to signal.

kMaximumBlinkMs.doc: Slowest blink period any rule may ask for. Past this the widget spends so long in one phase that it reads as one that failed to update.

kMaximumHoldMs.doc: Longest a styling rule, or a slot page raised by an event, may outlive the match that raised it. Past this it stops reading as a reaction to the car and starts reading as a stuck dashboard.

kMaximumGraphPoints.doc: Samples one graph retains. The ring buffer is sized by this whatever point_count asks for.

kMaximumGraphSources.doc: Telemetry sources one graph draws on a single plot, counting the widget's own. Each one costs a point array and an LVGL line of its own, which is why this is the smallest of the multi-source caps.

kMaximumGraphTraces.doc: Entries in a graph's traces array: kMaximumGraphSources less the one the widget's own source already is. An array capacity has to name a limit of its own, which is why the total is stated separately.

kMaximumTextSources.doc: Telemetry sources one text widget composes into a single string. Raising this grows the per-widget document storage, the widget render state, and the binder arrays.

kMaximumValueModifiers.doc: Value modifiers per text widget source.

kMaximumColorStops.doc: Stops in one widget colour ramp. Four is a normal, caution, warning and limit band, the same bands the conditional rules cover discretely.

kMaximumWidgetConditions.doc: Conditional styling rules per widget. Four covers a normal, caution, warning and limit band.

kMaximumSpriteFrames.doc: Frames one uploaded image may hold as a sprite sheet. A frame costs only its own pixels — every frame of a sheet is an offset into the one buffer the image was already loaded into — so this bounds what an author can address rather than what the device spends. Must match kMaximumSpriteFrames in the image contract.

kImageIdCapacity.doc: Uploaded image identifier storage including the terminator (31 usable bytes). Must match kImageIdCapacity in the image contract.

kWidgetIdCapacity.doc: Widget identifier storage including the terminator (15 usable bytes).

kWidgetTitleCapacity.doc: Widget title text storage including the terminator (15 usable bytes).

kUnavailableTextCapacity.doc: Placeholder text storage including the terminator (15 usable bytes).

kValidationPathCapacity.doc: Storage for the dotted property path reported with a rejection, including the terminator.

kValueBindingCapacity.doc: Canonical telemetry field name storage including the terminator (39 usable bytes). Must match CANONICAL_NAME_CAPACITY in tools/generate_telemetry_catalog.py.

kValueAffixCapacity.doc: Transform prefix and suffix storage including the terminator (15 usable bytes).

kTransparentColor.doc: Sentinel meaning no background is painted. Not representable in JSON; omit the property instead.

FontSpec.doc: Uploaded font asset reference. Resolution is exact; a missing family/size is a composition error.

TimeTransformConfig.doc: Stateless time formatting configuration owned by utils/transformers/time_transform.

NumberTransformConfig.doc: Stateless linear number formatting owned by utils/transformers/number_transform. The value is rendered as value * scale + offset with a fixed decimal count, which is how unit conversion is expressed; the device knows no unit names.

BoardId.doc: Immutable hardware identity. Must match the firmware build or the configuration is rejected.

TelemetryTransportId.doc: Telemetry transport selection. board_default defers to the immutable board descriptor.

TextAlignment.doc: Which point of a box the text is anchored to, on both axes. The unprefixed names are the middle row, so left, center and right sit vertically centred. Used for a text widget's value inside its content area and for a frame caption on its outer box.

ValueTransformType.doc: Presentation transform applied after the modifier pipeline.

GradientDirection.doc: Axis a linear gradient runs along. Only used when a gradient colour is set.

ColorRampTarget.doc: Which part of a widget the colour ramp paints. What content means is the widget type's own business: text paints its label, a bar its fill.

ConditionOperator.doc: Comparison a styling rule applies to the numeric value of its condition source.

WidgetActionType.doc: What a tap on a widget does. none is the default and leaves the object refusing input, which is what every widget did before actions existed.

ScreenTransition.doc: How the dashboard swaps one screen for another. slide is LVGL's animated screen load, the horizontal move a swipe reads as. none replaces the screen in a single frame: the animation composites both screens for its whole duration, which on a screen filled with widgets costs more per frame than either screen alone, so a dashboard that cannot afford it says so here rather than living with the drop.

ValueModifierType.doc: Stateful value processing implemented by a module behind the pipeline callback.

BarOrientation.doc: Axis a bar fills along. A vertical bar grows upwards unless it is inverted.

ShapeKind.doc: Outline a shape widget takes. A line is a thin rectangle, so it needs no kind of its own.

SlotTrigger.doc: How telemetry raises a slot page over the ones the tap cycles. none is a plain page reached only by tapping. value_changed raises it whenever the watched value differs from the last one seen, which is what makes a momentary aid such as ABS visible without naming a threshold. conditions raises it while one of its comparisons holds.

WidgetParentKind.doc: Which table parent_index addresses. Written by the parser, never authored: a widget names its parent by the index of the object that owns its coordinate space, and that object is a screen, a container shape, or one page of a slot.

WidgetType.doc: Widget kind discriminator. Selects the compile-time widget descriptor used to build the widget. The order of these values indexes the generated traits table and the parser table, so a new type is appended rather than inserted.

HardwareConfiguration.doc: Reserved bounded peripheral section. No user-configurable peripheral driver has a complete production contract yet, so a non-empty list is rejected rather than guessed.

WidgetPlacement.doc: Absolute geometry in logical screen pixels.

WidgetTitleStyle.doc: The caption on a widget's frame. It is anchored to a point on the widget's outer box, moved from there by the offsets, and it cuts the frame line on whichever border it ends up crossing.

fields.name: alignment
fields.doc: Which point of the widget's outer box the caption is anchored to before the offsets move it. The top and bottom rows straddle their border line, so the caption breaks it; the middle row sits inside the box and breaks nothing.

fields.name: border_gap
fields.doc: Cuts the border line where the caption crosses it. A caption that crosses no border cuts nothing.

fields.name: gap_padding_px
fields.doc: Clear space kept around the caption inside that cut, on every side. Bounded like the line it widens the mask over.

fields.name: alignment
fields.doc: Which point of the widget's content area the value label is anchored to.

fields.name: unavailable_text
fields.doc: Shown while the bound value is unavailable. Empty renders a zero through the widget's own transform, so a plain value reads 0 and a time value keeps its format.

ValueTransform.doc: Stateless presentation transform. Absent means no transform is applied. The prefix and suffix belong to the transform rather than to one type, so they also apply to an untransformed value.

ValueSourceConfiguration.doc: A canonical telemetry binding with its modifier pipeline, consumed as a typed value. Carries no transform: the widgets that read one map it through a range or compare it, rather than presenting it as text.

ColorStop.doc: One anchor of a colour ramp.

fields.name: at
fields.doc: Value of the watched source this colour lands exactly on. Absolute like a rule's value, not a fraction, so a ramp is authored in the units it is read in.

ColorRamp.doc: A colour interpolated from the watched source rather than switched by a threshold. It is the base layer: a matching rule paints over it, and with no stops the authored colour stands.

WidgetAction.doc: Navigation a tap performs. Carried by every widget, so a tap target is either a readout that doubles as a button or a rectangle of the screen — including an empty transparent shape, which is an invisible touch zone.

fields.name: screen
fields.doc: Target screen id for goto_screen. The other action types name no screen, and one that does is rejected rather than ignored. The composition resolves the id to an index once when it binds the tap, so a tap performs no name lookup.

WidgetCondition.doc: One styling rule. The first rule whose comparison holds describes the widget; whatever it leaves unset stays as the widget's static style, and a transparent colour means unset rather than see-through.

fields.name: blink_ms
fields.doc: Full blink period of the widget value. 0 renders steady.

fields.name: hold_ms
fields.doc: Keeps this rule applied for this long after it stops matching, so a momentary trigger such as traction control still produces a visible flash. 0 applies the rule only while it matches.

SlotCondition.doc: One activation rule for a slot page. The first rule whose comparison holds raises the page. Kept separate from a widget's styling rules because selection and appearance watch different fields; how long the page then stays up belongs to the page, not to the rule that raised it.

WidgetReference.doc: Declaration-order reference into the typed widget storage, held by whichever parent declared the widget. Carries the ordering keys so compositing needs no widget-type knowledge: z_index ascending, authored array order breaking ties. Declared before the widget structs because a container shape holds an array of these.

TextSourceConfiguration.doc: One canonical telemetry source of a text widget, consumed through a pre-bound typed callback. Its transform affixes are what separate it from the next source, so composing several needs no format string.

WidgetFrame.doc: What every widget type owns regardless of what it draws: where it sits, how it is boxed, and the rules that restyle it. Flattened into each widget, so these are plain widget properties on the wire.

fields.name: background_grad_color
fields.doc: Far end of a linear gradient across the background. Omitted paints the background flat.

fields.name: background_inset_px
fields.doc: Gap between the border and the painted background, so a filled widget keeps its frame visible. Applies to the authored background and to one a rule paints.

fields.name: screen_index
fields.doc: Screen this widget is parented to, written by the parser from the screen that declared it. An LVGL object has one parent, so a pool slot belongs to exactly one screen.

fields.name: parent_index
fields.doc: Index of the container this widget was authored inside, written by the parser. Which table it indexes is what parent_kind says: the shape pool, or the flat slot page table addressed as slot_pool_index * kMaximumSlotPages + page. A depth-first parse counts a container before its children, so a nested container's own index is always higher than its parent's — which is what makes a cycle unrepresentable.

fields.name: parent_kind
fields.doc: What owns this widget's coordinate space, written by the parser. screen means its geometry is absolute and parent_index is unused.

TextWidgetConfiguration.doc: Reusable telemetry text widget. Renders its ordered sources as one string.

ValueRange.doc: Input window a widget maps its source through. The fraction is clamped, so a value outside the window reads as full or empty rather than overflowing.

BarWidgetConfiguration.doc: One telemetry source drawn as a filled proportion of the widget. The frame background is the track the fill runs over, so a bar needs no track colour of its own.

fields.name: origin
fields.doc: Value the fill grows from, clamped into the range. Omitted means the low end, which is what a plain gauge wants; setting it to the middle of a signed range gives a centred meter such as a lap delta.

fields.name: inverted
fields.doc: Fills from the opposite end: right instead of left, or top instead of bottom.

fields.name: fill_grad_color
fields.doc: Far end of a linear gradient across the fill, running along the bar's own axis. Omitted paints the fill flat.

ArcWidgetConfiguration.doc: One telemetry source swept around an arc. The track is the arc's own background, so a gauge needs no shape behind it.

fields.name: start_angle_deg
fields.doc: Where the sweep begins, in LVGL degrees: zero is three o'clock and the angle grows clockwise.

fields.name: sweep_deg
fields.doc: How far the arc runs from its start. An extent rather than an end angle, so the wrap past 360 degrees is never ambiguous. A sweep of zero would draw nothing and one past a full turn would wrap over itself.

fields.name: thickness_px
fields.doc: Ring thickness. Two of these also have to fit across the widget, which the display-aware validator checks separately.

fields.name: track_color
fields.doc: Unfilled part of the sweep. Omitted leaves it unpainted, which suits an arc drawn over a shape.

fields.name: inverted
fields.doc: Sweeps from the far end of the arc instead of the near one.

IndicatorSegment.doc: One lamp in an indicator strip.

fields.name: threshold
fields.doc: Fraction of the widget's range, 0 to 1, at or above which this segment lights. A fraction rather than a raw value, so one authored strip suits any engine.

IndicatorWidgetConfiguration.doc: A row of lamps that light as one telemetry source climbs its range: shift lights, a rev strip, a stint marker.

fields.name: off_color
fields.doc: Colour of a segment that is not lit. Omitted leaves it unpainted.

fields.name: blink_threshold
fields.doc: Range fraction at or above which every lit segment blinks. The default is past the top of the range, which is how a strip says never.

fields.name: blink_ms
fields.doc: Blink period once the blink threshold is reached. Zero never blinks.

GraphTraceConfiguration.doc: A second or third source drawn on the same plot as the graph's own. It carries a window of its own, because a trace of speed beside one of throttle would otherwise flatten against an edge, and a colour of its own, because that is what tells the two apart.

GraphWidgetConfiguration.doc: A rolling trace of one telemetry source, plus up to two more drawn over the same plot. The history is presentation state the widget samples for itself; it is not a telemetry value and nothing else can read it.

fields.name: point_count
fields.doc: Samples the trace shows. The ring buffer is sized by kMaximumGraphPoints whatever this asks for, and every trace of one graph keeps the same count.

fields.name: sample_interval_ms
fields.doc: How often a sample is taken, which with point_count sets how far back the trace reaches. One clock for the whole widget, so the traces stay aligned along it.

fields.name: line_width_px
fields.doc: Thickness of every trace. Half of it is reserved inside the plot on each side, so a value at either end of its window is drawn whole rather than cut by the frame.

fields.name: traces
fields.doc: Further sources over the same plot, each with its own window and colour. The widget's own source is the first trace, so this holds one fewer than kMaximumGraphSources.

ImageWidgetConfiguration.doc: An uploaded image drawn inside the frame. Neither scaled nor rotated: the configurator converts each image to the size it is drawn at, which also keeps the accelerated draw path on the ESP32-P4. It binds telemetry only to choose between the frames of a sprite sheet; its styling rules can still hide it, flash it or recolour it.

fields.name: image
fields.doc: Identifier of an uploaded image. A missing one is a composition error, never a silent fallback — the same rule a font family follows.

fields.name: sprite_frame
fields.doc: Which frame of a sprite sheet to draw. A plain image holds the one frame, so this stays 0; a frame past what the sheet holds is a composition error, the same as naming an image that is not installed. Ignored when sprite_frame_source is given.

fields.name: sprite_frame_source
fields.doc: Telemetry that chooses the frame instead. The value is rounded to the nearest whole number and clamped to the frames the sheet holds, so a source that leaves the range picks the first or the last rather than drawing nothing. Rejected on an image whose asset has a single frame, so a binding never sits unread.

fields.name: recolor
fields.doc: Tints the image towards this colour. Omitted draws it as uploaded — except for an alpha8 image, which carries no colour of its own and is painted white until this says otherwise.

fields.name: recolor_opa
fields.doc: How strongly the recolour applies, 0 to 255. Does not apply to an alpha8 image: there the colour is the image's own, not a tint over one, so it is drawn at full strength whatever this says.

ShapeWidgetConfiguration.doc: Panels, dividers and backing plates, and the widget that draws while holding other widgets. The frame is the whole widget: it binds no telemetry of its own, but its styling rules can still hide it or flash it, and a line is a thin rectangle. A shape with widgets is a container — its children are placed relative to its box and cut off at it, unless clip_children says otherwise.

fields.name: clip_children
fields.doc: Cuts the widgets inside this shape off at its box, the way a panel holds what is on it. False draws them where they land instead, which is what a caption straddling a child's top border needs; the cost is paid in a wider invalidated area, measured from where the children actually reach. The shape's own border and caption are drawn by its parent and are never cut by this.

fields.name: widgets
fields.doc: Widgets authored inside this shape, parsed into the dashboard pool exactly as a screen's are. Their geometry is relative to this shape's box. A shape among them nests one level deeper, up to kMaximumNestingDepth.

SlotPageConfiguration.doc: One page of a slot: a set of widgets that share the slot's box and are shown or hidden together. A page has no geometry, no frame and no styling of its own — it is the slot's box, and its widgets are placed relative to it. Pages the tap cycles are the loop; a page with a trigger is raised over the loop while its event lasts, and the first such page in this array wins when several fire at once.

fields.name: in_loop
fields.doc: Includes this page in the sequence a tap cycles. A page left out of the loop is reachable only through its trigger, which is what an alert page wants.

fields.name: source
fields.doc: Telemetry this page watches. Required by both triggers and rejected without one, so a binding never sits unread.

fields.name: duration_ms
fields.doc: How long the page stays up after its event fires, after which the slot returns to whichever loop page was last selected. Required by value_changed, which would otherwise show a single frame; with conditions, 0 keeps the page up only while a rule holds. Bounded like a styling hold.

fields.name: widgets
fields.doc: Widgets authored on this page, parsed into the dashboard pool exactly as a screen's are. Their geometry is relative to the slot's box. A page costs no nesting level of its own, so these sit exactly where a container shape's children would: one below the slot, up to kMaximumNestingDepth.

SlotWidgetConfiguration.doc: An area of a screen that switches what it shows. It draws nothing of its own — no background, border, caption or styling rules, all of which are rejected rather than ignored — and exists only to hold pages. A tap cycles the pages in the loop; a page whose trigger fires is raised over them for its duration and then hands the slot back to the loop page that was showing. A slot is authored directly on a screen: it holds containers rather than living inside one.

fields.name: clip_children
fields.doc: Cuts the widgets on every page of this slot off at the slot's box. Not an appearance — a slot still draws nothing — but the same choice a container shape makes, because a page is an area of the screen in exactly the same way.

fields.name: pages
fields.doc: Pages this slot switches between, in priority order. At least one must be in the loop, so a slot always has something to fall back to.

ScreenConfiguration.doc: One dashboard screen: the coordinate space its widgets are placed in, and the order they stack in. The widgets themselves live in the dashboard's pool; a screen names them by reference. Widgets authored directly on the screen appear in its own reference table, and widgets authored inside a container shape appear in that shape's.

fields.name: widgets
fields.doc: Heterogeneous widget array discriminated by the type property. Each element is parsed into the dashboard pool for its variant, and the screen keeps a reference to that pool entry. This is the only array a slot may appear in: a slot is built before every container that could hold one, which is what keeps composition to one pass per type.

DashboardConfiguration.doc: Owns the typed widget storage as one pool shared by every screen; a screen holds only an ordered list of references into it. A screen therefore costs its reference table rather than a full set of widget arrays.

fields.name: transition
fields.doc: How every move between screens is drawn, whether a swipe or a tap asked for it. Dashboard-wide because an animation draws the screen being left as well as the one arriving, so a per-screen answer would only hold in one direction.

validation_errors.name: malformed
validation_errors.doc: Not parseable JSON, oversized payload, or trailing content.

validation_errors.name: unsupported_schema
validation_errors.doc: Stored record uses a schema version this firmware does not accept.

validation_errors.name: board_mismatch
validation_errors.doc: Board identifier does not match the firmware build.

validation_errors.name: invalid_hardware
validation_errors.doc: Hardware list is not an empty array.

validation_errors.name: invalid_transport
validation_errors.doc: Unknown transport or one the board does not support.

validation_errors.name: invalid_uart
validation_errors.doc: UART pins do not match the board or baud rate is out of range.

validation_errors.name: invalid_module
validation_errors.doc: Module section value out of range.

validation_errors.name: invalid_screen
validation_errors.doc: Screen section is malformed or the screen count is out of range.

validation_errors.name: invalid_dashboard
validation_errors.doc: Dashboard section is malformed or references an absent module.

validation_errors.name: invalid_widget
validation_errors.doc: Widget property is malformed, out of range, entirely off the display, or nested deeper than kMaximumNestingDepth.

validation_errors.name: invalid_slot
validation_errors.doc: Slot widget carries an appearance it has none of, was authored somewhere other than a screen, or holds no page the tap can reach.

validation_errors.name: invalid_slot_page
validation_errors.doc: Slot page is malformed, or its trigger and its source, rules and duration do not agree.

validation_errors.name: unknown_property
validation_errors.doc: Property name is not part of this schema version.

validation_errors.name: duplicate_property
validation_errors.doc: Property appears more than once in the same object.
